title.en: How we know about the past

text.en:
Hari found an old coin in his grandmother's trunk. It had strange letters and a king's head on it.
His teacher said, "Coins, tools, buildings and old writings are clues. Historians study them to learn about the past, like detectives."

History is the story of the past. We learn it from sources, which are clues left by people long ago.
Archaeological sources are things found under or on the ground: tools, pots, coins, jewellery, ruins of buildings and inscriptions carved on stone or metal.
Literary sources are things written: books, letters, manuscripts, records. Oral sources are stories, songs and sayings passed by word of mouth.
A timeline puts events in order of time. Years before the year 1 are marked BCE (Before Common Era) and are counted backwards; years after are CE (Common Era).
Historians compare many sources to find out what really happened, because one source may be wrong or one-sided.
History is the story of the past. We learn it from clues called sources.
Tools, coins, pots and ruins are archaeological sources. Writings on stone are inscriptions.
Books and manuscripts are written sources. Songs and stories passed by mouth are oral sources.
A timeline lists events in order. BCE years count backwards from year one, and CE years count forwards.

problem.en: Which comes earlier on a timeline: 500 BCE or 200 CE?

text.en: BCE years come before the year 1.

why.en: They are in the past before the common era.
It is in the common era.

prompt.en: A friend says history is only what is written in books. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Tools, coins, buildings and inscriptions also tell us about the past.
Songs and stories passed by word of mouth are sources too.

points.en: BCE years are counted backwards; CE years forwards.
